claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface and menu layouts are overly complicated, difficult to understand, and hard to navigate.

citations.review_text: THIS GAME IS TRASH. the menu system makes no sense. your stamina runs out faster than a 100 year old smokers would. and my god the f*king crafting system is just nonsensical as can be. -10/10.

Cheapo dayz copy. UI is very hard and not easy to understand for new players. Looting mechanisms are like copied out of 2011 dayz. Walking, running, everything is choppy and animations are not great.

In 94 minutes, here is what I did: Look for and eventually find two rocks. Made a knife that disappeared when I crafted it. Found it on the ground using tab button, eventually. Made a spear and a bow n arrows. Most of those got dropped too. Googled "how to find things on the ground in Scum". Navigate the many menu tabs. Figure out how to hold something. Ran around in circles hitting tab to try to find the stuff I dropped while crafting again. Finally craft a rag back pack out of my socks n underwear. Practice piss/poop/puke. Clicked refund. 

I thought I wanted this level of intricacy until I had it. I might try again another time, but right now I think the inventory management and working within this UI is going to be more work than I'm looking for.

ok this plays like unpolished ass.

Ok, as far as reading the comments about Scum, more details doesn't seem like it'll matter because these issues have been there for a long time. 

The control scheme - absolutely one of the worst i've ever played. It's so overly complicated that it's actually laughably bad.

The menu layout - this is part of the core of the game and yet, it's one of the worst UI layouts I've ever seen. There had to never been a meeting that said "Hey, maybe this is too much." 

The combat - given that I had very little experience with this, you can be stun locked, but the zombies cannot, so giving them 50 head shots while they claw your eyes out isn't fun.

I played less than two hours and returned it. It seems like there is a very fun game in there if you can get over the hurdle of mastering the labyrinthine user interface, playing inventory Tetris across multiple pockets and the ground, and a health system that makes you micromanage pooping. It took me several minutes to figure out how to bandage a wound, and that's with the AI tutor. And when I figured it out, it still took me several minutes to make the next bandage because, after cutting up all my clothing, I still didn't have enough rags. If feel like there's more than enough content in this game to keep players occupied without taking up so much of our time on metabolism and crafting very simple things. So if you're like me and like a game you can play with your dad, one that you can just pick up and play, 7 Days to Die is probably more your thing.

SCUM stands out as a deeply complex survival simulator, with its highly detailed metabolism, crafting, and character systems offering a level of realism rarely seen in the genre. Its large open world and sandbox freedom create a genuinely immersive and often unforgiving experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a complex metabolism and survival system that tracks body functions like vitamins and waste.

citations.review_text:
Not for me. Wanted to like this one, but it didn't land.

The environment feels flat and lifeless — for a survival game that's supposed to pull you in, the world just doesn't do it. On top of that, the gameplay is overcomplicated for no real reason. Systems stacked on systems that add friction without making the experience more fun. The metabolism management is the big one for me: tracking your body's inner workings in that much detail is tedious busywork, not depth. It doesn't make survival feel more real, it just makes it more of a chore.

The maps are also way bigger than they need to be. Huge open space for the sake of being huge, which mostly means a lot of empty travel time between anything actually happening.

There are much better survival games out there that respect your time and nail the core loop without burying it under needless complexity. If you want survival done well, look elsewhere.

EDIT: After playing for longer I feel the need to change some things in my review.

First of all: The game is badly optimized and will eat any GPU you throw at it. FSR is not working as intended as the developer replied but the real issue is the anti-aliasing making shadows & foliage flicker in distance giving the appearance of many small dots even at sg.AntiAliasingQuality=3 , so far it seems to be an issue for AMD GPU only so if you have NVIDIA GPU you should be okay.

If you can go past the stuttering, visual bugs, frame drops even on a high end rig then this game is a hidden gem. I have played many games including DayZ and none managed to get the feeling of 'being the only one left' in a zombie apocalypse like this game does. They really nailed the vibe, just find a bike and cycle around the map and you'll know what I mean, or find a bunker if you want the creepy & horror vibes. It is also extremely detailed and in-depth when it comes to survival mechanics, it's not just basic hunger and thirst, you have metabolism, vitamins, nutrients, you need to go pee or poop, there are so many things and small details which in my opinion makes it shine when compared to other survival games.

It is also by no means an easy game, you'll find yourself dying plenty of times. It really is an unique game and I hope they'll work on optimization and fixing the bugs, especially the visual bugs which in my opinion can really kill the experience this game can provide.

Tried to setup a brand new copy for a family member and the screen is misaligned and cant clicm on any button to adjust any settings. I gave this game so many second chances.

## The Good ##

What kept me playing was this huge payoff for the constant grind. This game is anything but casual. Enemies were very difficult to deal with at first. There were sicknesses to combat. Or just making sure you don't starve to death is something to figure out at first.
But if you do find that nice loot, you do see your money increase, you do build your first base, what a nice feeling!
If I hadn't found such a great PvE server, I would've quit way earlier.

## The Ugly ##

But the shortcomings are just ridiculous, sadly.

Frequent Crashes & Bugs:
I stopped counting how many times my game crashed in a "Fatal Error". If this happens in a fight or mid-flight, well, thanks for playing, try again. Updates introduce new bugs. Most of all, the devs just continue to fail at preventing these errors that just destroy gameplay.

Terrible In-Game Optimization:
The optimization is perhaps the worst I've ever encountered in any game. You can see my hardware specs. It's no gaming setup. Still, I can run every other game comfortably. But even on the lowest settings, I kept getting freezes for seconds. Mostly when aiming a bow. Consider this: an enemy is sprinting at you. You need to defend yourself, or else you're toast. You start aiming, and your game freezes for multiple seconds. How on Earth can this pass QA?
This is also the only game I've ever played that doesn't run on an HDD. Sure, long loading screens are common with HDDs. But it just froze so frequently that I had to switch to an SSD. Shows how incompetent the devs are.

Worst Update Process:
This is - again - the only game where installing some 2GB patch takes longer than downloading the whole 85GB. The devs just blame Steam for their update process. Strange, never saw another game on Steam taking over 1.5 hours to install a 2GB patch while maxing out my disk the whole time...

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features extensive survival and character management mechanics, including detailed health, metabolism, and crafting systems.

citations.review_text: SCUM is one of the most detailed and hardcore survival games available. It throws you onto a massive island where you have to scavenge, hunt, craft, build, fight, and make difficult decisions just to stay alive. What makes SCUM different from most survival games is how deeply it focuses on realism and character management.

Press S for SCUM.

Yet Another Love-Hate open world survival craft game but with a twist of The Running Man/Hunger Games/Battle Royale medley of flavors. And more. In that it's unexpectedly genius and dumb, and all various positions and emotions all rolled into one. Now, where to begin?

Background: prisoners are given an implant and parachuted onto an island for a TV show and must struggle to survive against the odds. That being other prisoners, zombies, mech robots, danger of nature/the elements, and your own body to stay maintained, to survive, make money, and accumulate "Fame" points to unlock better weapons and gear, and more. The island is full of nature and post-apocalyptic ruins, and is HUUUUUGE. You can hoof it for hours and barely scratch the surface. It's insane. You can go into every building, and everything is HIGHLY detailed. No "empty cube" rooms, but full of decor and detail, wreckage, destruction. There's small villas, towns, industrial outposts to cities.

Once on the ground, you need to find food, water, and build a shelter/base, and weapons, gear, and go around exploring/looting for whatever you can find to help make you more formidable. The game also "doesn't end". There is no "there can only be one", and it's not a "match" to play. It's very much a non-linear "HERE YA GO! *PLOP!*" and prisoners continually dumped on the island are left to their own devices. You know, like Australia. The game features a few "safe zones" which are small protected towns with vendors and various shops, including a bank, saloon, hospital, barber...and MORE.

The game is co-op/online with other players OR you can totally just play it in an offline/Singleplayer mode. The game world is already designed to be PVE, so you don't lose any features or anything by playing Singleplayer except that you're going through the experience solo.

Crafting...it sucks in this game, in that it's a bid unconventional and very difficult. This is probably where it would help to have frien…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that mechs can shoot through hills and walls from excessive ranges.

citations.review_text: Mechs are absolutely broken and shoot through hills, walls, and ridiculous ranges. Not to mention characters glitch and health issues stick regardless of treating the wounds. There's a lot of very bad bugs in this. Could be a great game if they actually put more effort into it.

[h2]Needs to go back to Early Access[/h2]
This game is incredibly unpolished. It honestly looks like the developers lacked the technical skills to handle complex looting, crafting, and vehicle driving systems. In its current state, this game should absolutely still be in Early Access.

[b]Examples of major issues:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Terrible Inventory Management:[/b] There is no quick-transfer feature for items between containers. You have to manually drag and drop everything with your mouse, which is awful considering there is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of loot in this game. There is also no auto-stacking for identical items—again, manual dragging is required.
[*] [b]Multiplayer Desync:[/b] Huge synchronization issues with containers in co-op. Items that have already been looted by another player still show up in my container. I can see them, but I can't drag them (annoying ghost item bug).
[*] [b]Zero Vehicle Physics:[/b] Collision physics for vehicles basically don't exist. You smash hard into something and there's no physical impact at all, yet the car still magically takes damage.
[*] [b]Clunky Combat:[/b] Both the shooting and melee mechanics feel completely wooden and stiff.
[*] [b]Empty & Repetitive World:[/b] The world feels completely lifeless and empty. The game relies heavily on repetitive assets and copy-pasted buildings. Walking through the city gives you the constant feeling that you are stuck in the exact same spot.
[/list]

[h3]Pricing is a joke[/h3]

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that the game features a deep metabolism system that tracks hunger, thirst, injuries, and body weight.

citations.review_text:
Short version:

Overall, it's a solid and well-rounded game.

The first few hours can be rough. There is a fairly steep learning curve when it comes to dealing with zombies, and NPCs can be unforgiving if you play too aggressively. This is not a game where you're an unstoppable action hero. Your character is vulnerable, and a run-and-gun playstyle will usually end badly.

More details:

Once you've learned the basics, both zombies and NPCs become much easier to handle. The game aims for a realistic survival experience. Guns are loud and attract attention, injuries matter, carrying too much weight slows you down, and you'll need to manage fatigue, hunger, and thirst.

For new players, I'd strongly recommend watching a quick 10-minute beginner guide on YouTube. If you'd rather learn by doing, focus on getting a bow early, avoid fighting more than one zombie at a time, and stay away from NPCs until you've acquired a firearm and some armour. Hunger is rarely an immediate problem, but thirst can become critical very quickly. Also, make sure to treat your wounds properly to avoid infection.

Performance

Performance is generally very good. Even on an RTX 4070 at 5120×1440 (Dual QHD), the game runs well. With a few settings turned down, you can expect roughly 80-110 FPS.

Depending on the server, you may occasionally encounter lag spikes. Pick a server with the lowest possible ping. For beginners, an official beginner server is usually the best choice, and servers with fewer players tend to provide a smoother and more relaxed experience.

Do you need any DLC?

No. Most DLC packs are purely cosmetic and can safely be ignored.

The only DLC I would consider for new players is the SCUM Deluxe Content Pack. It provides a few useful starter items, including extra water and a better backpack, which can make the early game a little more forgiving. While it's not required, it can give beginners a noticeably easier start.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that when a character dies, the body and equipped items can sometimes disappear completely, preventing players from recovering their gear.

citations.review_text:
I've played quite a bit to get a feel for the game.
I've enjoyed getting to know it more over time. It certainly has been engaging.

The reason for the negative review howerever is due to a serious bug that the devs seem unable to fix.
Sometimes when you die you cannot recover your body.
It just isn't there.  You get your weapons (what was in your hands / back holster slots) but the body itself is just gone.

I've had it happen repeatedly around bunkers.  I have lost multiple sets of full gear.
Given you are starting to do bunkers for the best gear and memory modules etc.  It is incredibly disheartening. Particularly starting out trying to learn this incredibly dangerous POI. 

Knowing you dont' just risk failing, but losing everything if you die.  
It's just not worth it.  

I know there are a lot of community suggestions for this. 
Log out at the death site.. restart the dedicated server.  See if others can see the body.  Look around in widening circles on the ground above where you died underground in bunker.   
For such a major issue as losing all items, I'm surprised it hasnt' been fixed.

Uninstalled after 1400 hours, when re-trying after a long break. Another game with great potential destroyed by it's devs.

The playerbase on PvP-Servers consists of 80% cheaters, 15% safezone campers and 5% actual survival players. There is no report function for players in the game, for the fact alone that the game doesn't even tell you who killed you in the first place. Realism over game necessity.

The good:
Nice graphics, nice atmosphere, nice setting, nice survival principles.

The bad:

Building a base is very time-consuming and useless, because you can't spawn at it unless you buy gold in the safezones. Which costs a lot of money, which means you will sell almost everything you find, just to be able to use your own base. Which leads to people camping the safezones, which always have very tight entry points and you can build very close to them too. In fact you won't even be able to spawn "close" to your body without having money in your bank account (yes, ultra-realistic about deaths, but then you need a bank account to be able to be cloned and thrown off a plane again). Most of the time you'll spawn on the other side of the map and it will take you an hour to get back into your area again - if you can dodge everything in your path there.

The ugly:
All changes since they've introduced modular cars have made the game worse. Bunkers were fun, now most of them are "abandoned" which means every (!) sound you make will spawn special zombies out of airvents - without limit. No matter how many of these you kill, you can never clear that bunker. (Worsts game mechanic I have faced in ANY game in my 35y of PC gaming.) The few normal bunkers left are forced action zones now, meaning everyone will try to get into these few, which bottlenecks players into a tiny amount of places on a huge map. (Bad game design.)

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the learning curve as steep and demanding for new players entering the survival systems.

citations.review_text:
SCUM is one of my favorite survival games because it gives you enough freedom to make every session feel different. You can spend hours scavenging abandoned towns, hunting for supplies, building a base, exploring the map, fighting other players, or just trying to stay alive long enough to get properly equipped.

Managing food, stamina, injuries, equipment and resources makes even simple trips feel meaningful. You’re constantly making decisions about what to carry, where to go and how much risk you’re willing to take.

There’s also something incredibly satisfying about slowly building yourself up from having practically nothing to becoming fully equipped and capable of taking on almost anything the island throws at you.

It can be rough around the edges, and the learning curve is definitely there, but the combination of survival, exploration, looting and PvP creates the kind of gameplay loop that can keep you occupied for hundreds of hours.

Steep learning curve for new players. New devs taking entire gameplay more serious and to new levels over previous (recent) devs. Not many rivals to open-world zombie survival scenario, includes sandbox (single player) for testing and messing about. Needs ability for games mods - would take this to new levels but will likely end up on console with pay to win servers. Most current DLC is not pay to win.

I used to love playing SCUM, I played for thousands of hours even with the game issues, because it was FUN and a challenge, now I don't.

Ever since the Jagex corporate takeover in 2023 SCUM play has been going to crap. They essentially forced Tomislav out in 2025 which took away the vision and goals of what SCUM was and was supposed to become. They then created the alot of the current mess of a game by changing an amazing though still buggy game to a game geared mainly towards lining their own pockets while doing the minimum they had to do to fix as little as possible.

Then at the end of 2025 Splash Damage acquired the game from Jagex and SCUM became the complete turd that it is now. They almost immediately went to pure profit mode and basically made the game look fun and flashy to make as much profit as quick as possible while burning the game down in the process. Runs slow, crashes alot...who cares we will make an expansion that looks cool and distracts everyone. Game bugs? Who cares, we can sell DLCs that make the players forget the crappy game play. Pretty low opinion of most of your player base that you profess to care so much about. The only player base you care about are the players who spend and even them not so much. 

The ironic part is that buying DLCs was originally there to help with the cost of developing the game and fixing things and many were happy to buy them and enjoy those extras while the game itself got better! Now though its just to make money with no true development, no actual fixing of any issues and certainly not getting better!

SCUM will never be what it was and it will never be what it was created to be but MAYBE you can get back some of the Hordes who have left if you actually fix the game issues...though I doubt either of those things will happen.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing fatal errors and crashes when driving vehicles or flying planes at high speeds along winding roads.

citations.review_text:
Scum is a very challenging but rewarding game. You are a criminal who has been parachuted on to an Island for a Hunger Games senario. I am on Skynett a PVE server. Choosing the correct server for your play style will save you months down the line.

Unfortunately it suffers from a lot of fatal errors, so flying planes or driving vehicles through winding roads at speed can lead to the death of your character, losing money and fame. (edit Aug 26) I have recently found out that the appdata\local\scum folder becomes corrupt on occasion. To cure this. Log out remove the folder and choose DX12 on start up of the game.

Bad bits
So Gamepires want to make a zombie survival game more kid friendly. Not sure why they would offer a game to all generations where NPCS want to kill you and loot you, and Zombies want to tear the flesh from your bones. Gamepires you had a great thing going, sensoring the great features that made us all laugh on downtime from quests and looting is not a great idea. At least leave it as an option for private servers to turn on or off. Take the fun away and you may lose your current playerbase.
7/10. Can be a really fun game, but. Early game is a walking and lying down simulator with some fatal errors tossed in.
